captions.detailed: This 3D model represents a flat, five-pointed pentagram star designed to be used as a Christmas tree topper. It is constructed from five interlocking, thin rectangular segments that form the classic self-intersecting star pattern. A circular mounting hole is drilled horizontally through one of the inner intersections near the base, allowing it to be secured to the tip of a tree.
captions.instruction: Create a parametric pentagram tree topper in OpenSCAD. The design should allow the user to adjust the side length, thickness, height, and the mounting hole diameter using custom parameters, ensuring the five segments are mathematically aligned and rotated to form a perfect star.
captions.factory: The script defines a 'side' module using a cube with mitered ends cut off at a 36-degree angle using rotated cubes in a difference operation. Five of these side modules are rotated and translated in a for-loop to form the pentagram. A horizontal cylinder is then subtracted from the assembly using a difference operation to create a mounting hole of the specified diameter.
